target.title: fix(android): show specific gateway auth-recovery reason instead of generic label
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related #98046. During Android gateway setup/reconnect, `gatewaySummary()` (Overview screen /
Settings row) and `gatewayStatusLabel()` (Gateway settings metric) collapse every auth failure
into one generic **"Authentication needed"** label — whether the setup QR expired, a token/password
is missing or invalid, or the saved device identity is stale. Users cannot distinguish an expired
setup code from an invalid or stale saved credential in these two UI surfaces.

This covers only the Overview and Settings screens. #98094 (merged) / #98275 / #98280 already
cover the same issue's Onboarding/Recovery-screen copy (`OnboardingFlow.kt`) — a different
user-visible surface than this PR touches.

## Why This Change Was Made

Client-only change — no gateway protocol, config, or wire-format change. `MainViewModel.
gatewayConnectionProblem: StateFlow<GatewayConnectionProblem?>` already carries a machine-readable
`code` from the gateway's auth-reject response (`AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_INVALID`,
`AUTH_TOKEN_MISSING`, `AUTH_PASSWORD_MISSING`, `AUTH_PASSWORD_MISMATCH`,
`AUTH_TOKEN_MISMATCH`/`AUTH_DEVICE_TOKEN_MISMATCH`,
`CONTROL_UI_DEVICE_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`/`DEVICE_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`), already consumed by
`recoveryGatewayAuthDetail()` on the Onboarding/Recovery screen, but the Overview and Settings
screens never received it and fell back to a plain substring match on `statusText`. This threads
the existing signal into both functions via a shared `gatewayAuthNeededSummary()` helper with
short, code-specific labels, wiring `viewModel.gatewayConnectionProblem` into the three call sites
that already have `viewModel` in scope. The iOS app already solved the same problem with an
equivalent `GatewayConnectionIssue` enum derived from the same problem shape.

## User Impact

- Overview screen, Settings "Gateway" row, and Settings → Gateway → Status metric now show
  specific recovery guidance (e.g. "Setup code expired", "Gateway token needed", "Saved auth
  invalid", "Device identity required") instead of a generic "Authentication needed" whenever the
  gateway has already reported *why* auth failed.
- Falls back to the previous generic "Authentication needed" label when no recognized problem
  code is present. Non-auth states (connecting, pairing, TLS, certificate) are unaffected.

## Evidence

`gatewaySummary()` and `gatewayStatusLabel()` were promoted from `private` to `internal` (this
file's existing pattern for JVM-unit-tested logic, e.g. `overviewHeaderState`), with new
deterministic tests per auth code, a null/unrecognized-code fallback, unrelated-state
non-interference, and two tests per file using the exact real server message text (`src/gateway/
server/ws-connection/auth-messages.ts` and `message-handler.ts`) rather than only synthetic
strings.

Gradle JVM unit tests, rebased on `upstream/main` @ `adcfebc276`:

```
$ ./gradlew :app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest \
    --tests "ai.openclaw.app.ui.ShellScreenLogicTest" \
    --tests "ai.openclaw.app.ui.SettingsScreensTest" --rerun-tasks

BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 14s
ShellScreenLogicTest: tests=25 failures=0 errors=0 skipped=0
SettingsScreensTest:  tests=6  failures=0 errors=0 skipped=0
```

`./gradlew :app:ktlintCheck` — the touched files (`ShellScreen.kt`, `SettingsScreens.kt`,
`ShellScreenLogicTest.kt`, `SettingsScreensTest.kt`) are clean. 5 pre-existing violations remain
in three unrelated files (`GatewayExecApprovals.kt`, `ClawSurfaces.kt`, `OnboardingFlow.kt`), none
touched by this diff.

`autoreview` (Codex, `--mode branch --base upstream/main`): clean, no accepted/actionable
findings, `overall: patch is correct (0.86)`.

target.title: feat(context-engine): add reference context channel
target.body:
Closes #88753

## What Problem This Solves

Context-engine authors need a safe way to provide historical summaries, memories, or retrieved context without encoding that data as fresh user messages or higher-authority prompt additions. Without a dedicated lane, compacted/reference data can regain too much prompt authority or interfere with provider message constraints.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a narrow `AssembleResult.referenceContext` SDK lane plus a `reference-context` host capability. Embedded and Codex app-server hosts validate the shape, then render the items through host-owned lower-authority reference blocks instead of letting engines smuggle reference data into executable conversation history.

## User Impact

Context-engine and plugin developers can now return historical/reference data separately from model-history messages. Users get safer continuity because historical summaries are explicitly framed as quoted lower-authority context, not as a new user turn or new instruction.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/context-engine/reference-context.test.ts`

target.title: fix(feishu): bound Feishu API JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## Summary

- Adds a shared Feishu JSON response wrapper that delegates to `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http` while capping credentialed Feishu API JSON bodies at 16 MiB.
- Routes app-registration JSON reads through the shared helper, covering init, device-code begin, polling, and app-owner lookup.
- Extends the same cap to the sibling streaming-card token and card-create JSON reads, addressing the previous review finding about an uncovered Feishu credentialed path.
- Adds an optional `fetchImpl`/`lookupFn` test seam to the app-registration and streaming-card fetch call sites so tests can exercise the real `fetchWithSsrFGuard` guard end-to-end instead of replacing it with a mock; production callers are unaffected (no caller passes these options, so default behavior is unchanged).
- Rebases cleanly onto latest `upstream/main` and keeps the upstream scan-to-create QR terminal rendering test.

## Linked context

No linked issue; this is a bounded-response-read hardening follow-up for Feishu/Lark credentialed API JSON responses.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Feishu app-registration and streaming-card credentialed API paths previously had successful JSON reads that could buffer an unbounded response body.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86-64, local OpenClaw repo environment, real `ReadableStream`/`Response` body paths through production functions, real `fetchWithSsrFGuard` guard (not a mocked wrapper) with only the final socket hop redirected to a local `node:http` server.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts -- --run
  oxlint extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.ts extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts \
    extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts \
    extensions/feishu/src/json-response.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: Live terminal output from real node:http server tests (no fetch mock, real SSRF guard):
  ```text
  [feishu fetchFeishuJson bound proof] real-ssrf-guard: guarded_url=https://accounts.feishu.cn/oauth/v1/app/registration socket=127.0.0.1
   ✓ Feishu app registration > sends bound reads through the real SSRF guard before local socket redirect
   ✓ feishu bound reads — local HTTP server > rejects oversized response before fully buffering the response (OOM guard)
   ✓ feishu bound reads — local HTTP server > parses well-formed JSON response under the cap
  [feishu fetchFeishuJson bound proof] over-cap: bytes_pulled=18874368 cap=16777216 canceled=true
  [feishu fetchFeishuJson bound proof] under-cap: returned={"deviceCode":"dev-code-123","userCode":"UC-456","interval":5,"expireIn":300}
  [bound-proof] canceled at 18/20 chunks
  Test Files  2 passed (2)
       Tests  29 passed (29)
  ```
  The first line shows `fetchWithSsrFGuard` invoked with the real production Feishu hostname (`accounts.feishu.cn`) while only the final socket connects to `127.0.0.1` — the real hostname allowlist/DNS-pinning policy path executes, not a stand-in. Over-cap read canceled at 18874368 bytes (cap 16777216); under-cap returns expected parsed JSON; stream canceled at chunk 18/20, confirming early cancellation before full buffering.
- **Observed result after fix:** App-registration oversized JSON rejects with `feishu.api: JSON response exceeds ...`; malformed JSON is labelled `feishu.api`; streaming-card token and card-create oversized JSON reject with their own call-site labels and cancel the stream before reading the full body. Normal under-cap app-registration and streaming-card flows still parse and pass existing tests.
- **What was not tested:** Live Feishu/Lark tenant calls with real app credentials. No tenant credentials are available in this environment.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** Tests inject a `fetchImpl` (redirects only the final socket to a local `node:http` server) and a hermetic `lookupFn` (avoids real DNS resolution) into the real, unmocked `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call — the guard's hostname allowlist/DNS-pinning logic runs for real against the actual Feishu/Lark hostnames. This is a stronger proof than the previous version, which replaced `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with a `vi.fn()` mock and never exercised the guard itself. No Feishu credentials or external network required; this proves the bound-read and SSRF-guard code paths, not Feishu-specific response content.
- **Before evidence:** Previous branch was conflicting against main and only covered app-registration. The sibling `streaming-card.ts` token reader remained a bare JSON reader before this update. An earlier proof revision replaced `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with a full mock rather than exercising it for real.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts -- --run` — 2 files, 29 tests passed.
- `oxlint extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.ts extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/json-response.ts` — 0 problems.
- Merge conflict with the upstream QR rendering test resolved; that test remains in this branch.

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? **Only for oversized successful Feishu/Lark JSON responses**: they now fail closed at 16 MiB instead of being read unbounded.
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? **No**
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? **No** — the same endpoints, headers, and token cache semantics are used; the new `fetchImpl`/`lookupFn` parameters are optional test-only seams with no effect when omitted (all production call sites omit them).
- What is the highest-risk area? Maintainer acceptance of a 16 MiB fail-closed cap on Feishu control-plane JSON responses.
- How is that risk mitigated? These responses are control-plane/token/app metadata payloads and should be tiny relative to 16 MiB; under-cap and existing streaming-card tests verify normal behavior remains intact.

## Current review state

- **Next action:** ClawSweeper re-review, then maintainer review if CI stays green.
- **Waiting on:** CI after rebase/push.
- **Bot/reviewer comments addressed:** Resolved merge conflict; covered the sibling `streaming-card.ts` Feishu token/card-create JSON readers; changed the Feishu wrapper to delegate to shared `readProviderJsonResponse`; kept upstream QR rendering test; replaced the mocked `fetchWithSsrFGuard` test double with a real-guard proof (only the final socket hop and DNS lookup are test-injected) matching the proof style already accepted on sibling bound-read PRs in this repository.

target.title: fix(cron): preserve numeric delivery thread id across SQLite round-trip
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A cron job's delivery target can carry a `threadId` that is legitimately either a string or a number (`string | number`). The input schema (`src/cron/delivery-field-schemas.ts`) accepts `z.union([TrimmedNonEmptyStringFieldSchema, z.number().finite()])` and `normalizeCronJobInput` deliberately preserves a numeric thread id. Numeric thread ids are real: for example a Telegram forum/topic id like `1008013`.

The SQLite codec collapses that type. On write it stores the thread id as TEXT via `String(...)`, and on read it hands the raw TEXT column straight back:

```ts
// src/cron/store/delivery-codec.ts write path
delivery_thread_id:
  delivery?.threadId === undefined || delivery.threadId === null
    ? null
    : String(delivery.threadId),

// src/cron/store/delivery-codec.ts read path (before)
...(row.delivery_thread_id ? { threadId: row.delivery_thread_id } : {}),
```

So a persistence round-trip silently changes the type:

```
INPUT  threadId: 1008013   (number)
LOADED threadId: "1008013" (string)
```

This matters because the reloaded value is what the live delivery path consumes. `resolveCronDeliveryPlan` runs it through `normalizeOptionalThreadValue`, which keeps the string-vs-number distinction rather than re-normalizing it. A freshly created in-memory job carries `threadId: 1008013` (number); the same job after a save/reload carries `"1008013"` (string). Identical config produces two different runtime types depending on whether the job came from disk or memory. Some channel adapters re-coerce (Telegram's `parseTelegramThreadId` accepts both), but others require a number: the Telegram native approval path only sets `messageThreadId` when `typeof threadId === "number"` (`extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.ts`), so a reloaded string-typed topic id is dropped there.

## Why This Change Was Made

The column is TEXT, so both `1008013` and `"1008013"` are already stored as the same bytes; the fix belongs on the read boundary that reconstructs the runtime value. `deliveryFromRow` is the single persistence read surface (the config sidecar in `row-codec.ts` is projected from it), so fixing it there aligns both the store and sidecar copies of a job.

```ts
// src/cron/store/delivery-codec.ts (after)
function threadIdFromColumn(value: string): string | number {
  const numeric = Number(value);
  return Number.isSafeInteger(numeric) && String(numeric) === value ? numeric : value;
}
// ...
...(row.delivery_thread_id ? { threadId: threadIdFromColumn(row.delivery_thread_id) } : {}),
```

A stored value is reconstructed as a number only when it is the canonical decimal form of a safe integer (`String(Number(value)) === value`). This matches the truncated-integer contract of `normalizeOptionalThreadValue` and is lossless for every non-canonical string: `"007"`, `"1e3"`, `"12.5"`, `"topic-9"`, and any non-numeric id stay strings and round-trip unchanged. The write path stays `String(...)`, which is correct for a TEXT column. No schema change or migration is needed, and existing persisted rows benefit immediately.

## User Impact

Cron jobs configured with a numeric delivery thread id (for example a Telegram forum/topic id) now deliver to the same thread whether the job is served from memory or reloaded from SQLite. Previously a save/reload silently retyped the id to a string, which downstream paths that require a numeric thread id (such as Telegram native approval delivery) would drop, sending to the general chat instead of the topic.

## Evidence

Verification:
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/cron/store/delivery-codec.ts src/cron/store.test.ts` -> clean.
- `oxfmt --check src/cron/store/delivery-codec.ts src/cron/store.test.ts` -> clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` -> no errors.
- Added colocated regression tests in `src/cron/store.test.ts` (numeric thread id reloads as a number; non-numeric `"007"` stays a string). vitest could not be run in this checkout (worker startup is killed by the sandbox resource governor); the same save/load assertions are demonstrated live below and the tests run in CI.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: a numeric cron delivery thread id (e.g. Telegram topic id 1008013) is retyped to a string by a SQLite save/reload, diverging from the same job held in memory.
Real environment tested: drove the real `saveCronStore`/`loadCronStore` from `src/cron/store.ts` and the real `resolveCronDeliveryPlan` from `src/cron/delivery-plan.ts` against a real temp SQLite state DB (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`), on pristine main and on the patched tree. Nothing was stubbed: the real codec, the real Kysely store, and the real delivery-plan resolver all ran; only the state directory was a throwaway temp dir.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: create a job with `delivery.threadId: 1008013` (number) and a second job with `delivery.threadId: "007"` (string), `saveCronStore`, then `loadCronStore`, and inspect the reloaded delivery thread id plus `resolveCronDeliveryPlan(job).threadId`.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main delivery-codec.ts)
numeric input  threadId: 1008013 (number)
numeric loaded threadId: "1008013" string
numeric plan   threadId: "1008013" string
numeric matches in-memory job: false
string  input  threadId: "007" (string)
string  loaded threadId: "007" string
# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
numeric input  threadId: 1008013 (number)
numeric loaded threadId: 1008013 number
numeric plan   threadId: 1008013 number
numeric matches in-memory job: true
string  input  threadId: "007" (string)
string  loaded threadId: "007" string
```
Observed result after fix: the reloaded numeric thread id and the resolved delivery-plan thread id come back as the number 1008013 and match the in-memory job, while the non-numeric "007" id stays a string, so the persistence round-trip no longer changes the value's type.
What was not tested: no live Telegram send (the downstream drop is shown by reading `approval-handler.runtime.ts`, not by a live topic post); vitest and full build were not run in this checkout.

target.title: fix(google): bound OAuth token error body reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `requestTokenGrant` helper in the Google OAuth token exchange path read error response bodies via `response.text()` without any size cap. A misconfigured or malfunctioning Google OAuth endpoint (or intermediate proxy) that returns an oversized error body — e.g. a misrouted HTML page or a proxy error splash — could exhaust gateway memory before the error was surfaced.

The `fetchWithTimeout` wrapper in `oauth.http.ts` already bounds the response at 16 MiB, so the raw body cannot overflow memory. However, an unbounded 16 MiB error body can still be embedded verbatim into the downstream `Error` message, producing excessive log payloads and redundant memory pressure.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Error path** (`response.status !== 200`): replace `response.text()` with `readResponseTextLimited(response, 8 KiB)`. Consistent with `DISCORD_API_ERROR_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES` in `extensions/discord/src/api.ts`. The cap is generous for a structured OAuth error payload (~100 bytes of JSON) while keeping a runaway HTML page from polluting downstream diagnostics.

- **Success path**: replace the bare `(await response.json()) as {…}` cast with `readProviderJsonResponse<T>(response, …)`. The upstream `fetchWithTimeout` already bounds the body at 16 MiB, so this is defense-in-depth type-safe parsing with a consistent provider error surface.

No new dependencies, APIs, config keys, or protocol changes.

## User Impact

Normal OAuth errors (invalid grant, expired token, etc.) preserve their complete diagnostic payload. Oversized error streams are truncated at 8 KiB — the error message still identifies the failure, and the upstream 16 MiB bound ensures memory safety at the transport layer.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: unbounded `response.text()` on error path → bounded `readResponseTextLimited(8 KiB)`
- **Real environment tested**: loopback HTTP server (`node:http.createServer`) streaming 1 MiB of chunked body over `127.0.0.1`, driven through the exported `exchangeCodeForTokens` and `refreshTokensForGeminiCli` public APIs with mocked `fetchWithTimeout`
- **Exact steps**:
  1. Start a loopback HTTP server that streams a 1 MiB error body (4 KiB chunks, 2 ms delay, no Content-Length)
  2. Mock `fetchWithTimeout` to return the loopback Response
  3. Call `exchangeCodeForTokens("test-code", "test-verifier")`
  4. Assert the error message is bounded (≈8 KiB text)
  5. Assert the stream was cancelled before the server finished writing (proof the read stopped early)
  6. Positive control: a small valid OAuth error body (`{"error":"invalid_grant"}`) is preserved exactly
  7. Both `exchangeCodeForTokens` (authorization code) and `refreshTokensForGeminiCli` (refresh) paths are covered
- **Observed result**: `[google oauth.token loopback proof] oversized path: cap=8192 streamed=1048576 message_length=8215`
- **What was not tested**: The full end-to-end path through Google's actual OAuth endpoint (SSRF guard + DNS pinning). The `fetchWithTimeout` wrapper already has an independent 16 MiB bound; this PR adds a tighter text cap at the call site.

### Validation Evidence

```
pnpm test extensions/google/oauth.token.test.ts

✓ bounds oversized OAuth error body text
✓ preserves complete small error body text within the limit
✓ bounds oversized OAuth error body text during token refresh

Mutation proof:
  $ git stash      → 2 FAILED (old code buffers full body, stream not cancelled)
  $ git stash pop  → 3 PASSED
```

### Security & Privacy / Compatibility

- Cap value (8 KiB) matches existing `DISCORD_API_ERROR_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES` convention
- `readResponseTextLimited` reads at most maxBytes from the stream; oversized bodies are truncated, not silently consumed
- OAuth tokens, client secrets, and user credentials are not exposed in the capped error path
- No config, dependency, protocol, or `CHANGELOG.md` changes

---

_AI-assisted._

target.title: fix(imessage): shed emoji anywhere in poll-vote echo match
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native iMessage poll support merged in #98421, including a `poll_vote_echo` guard
that suppresses the redundant one-word text the agent tends to send right after
voting (it already shows on the poll) under `message_tool_only` reply mode.

That guard leaks for any poll whose option carries an emoji. iMessage stores
native poll options with a **trailing** emoji, e.g. `"Lobster 🦞 "`, while the
agent echoes its vote with a **leading** emoji, e.g. `"🦞 Lobster."`. The guard's
`normalizePollEchoText` stripped only a *leading* emoji prefix, so the option
normalized to `"lobster 🦞"` but the echo to `"lobster"` — no match, and the
redundant text went out anyway. Plain-word options (`"Blue"`) were unaffected,
which is why it slipped through review.

Confirmed from live `chat.db` on macOS 26.4.1: the option balloon decoded to
`["Lobster 🦞 ", "Crab 🦀 ", "Shrimp 🦐 "]`, and the leaked reply row decoded to
`"🦞 Lobster."`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The normalizer now sheds emoji **anywhere**, not just a leading prefix, across
every emoji class so both sides of the comparison shed them symmetrically:

- Pictographic (🦞) — the reported case
- Regional-indicator **flags** (🇺🇸) and subdivision-flag tag chars — these are
  *not* `Extended_Pictographic`, so they need their own ranges
- **Keycap** sequences (`1️⃣`) cleared as a unit, so an emoji-only keycap label
  normalizes to empty instead of leaving a stray `"1"`
- ZWJ / skin-tone combiners

Internal punctuation is preserved, so `C#`, `C++`, `Node.js` stay distinct. An
emoji-only label normalizes to empty and the guard's existing non-empty-option
check fails open (never wrongly suppresses).

## User Impact

- Voting on an iMessage poll whose options include emoji (the common case —
  iMessage's own UI encourages emoji options) no longer produces a redundant
  one-word text next to the vote.
- No behavior change for plain-word options, non-poll sends, or any text that
  adds content beyond the bare option label.
- No config or API surface change.

## Evidence

- New unit test `src/agents/tools/message-tool.poll-echo.test.ts` — 5 passing,
  covering the emoji-suffix/prefix match, regional-indicator flags, subdivision
  tags, ZWJ/skin-tone, keycap-as-unit, keycap-empty, plain-digit/`#` preservation,
  and `C#`/`C++`/`Node.js`.
- `src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts` "poll vote echo guard" — 8 passing,
  including a new integration test casting a vote whose resolved option is
  `"Lobster 🦞 "` then sending `"🦞 Lobster."` and asserting `status:suppressed`,
  `reason:poll_vote_echo`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — clean.
- Independent Codex review (gpt-5.4): first pass flagged the flag + keycap gaps;
  after hardening, re-review **READY** with no remaining findings.
- Live on macOS 26.4.1: the fix is deployed on the running gateway and suppresses
  the `"🦞 Lobster."` echo end-to-end.

### Before/after proof (real data, both function versions run verbatim)

Runs the actual `normalizePollEchoText` source from **`origin/main` (buggy)** and
this branch, against the exact strings captured from `chat.db` (poll balloon
`"Lobster 🦞 "`, leaked reply `"🦞 Lobster."`), through the guard's real
comparison (`outboundText && norm(option) && norm(text) === norm(option)`):

```
case                                     main         fix
--------------------------------------------------------------------
LIVE bug (crustacean)                    leaked       SUPPRESSED   <-- FIXED
control: plain word ("Blue")             SUPPRESSED   SUPPRESSED
flag option ("USA 🇺🇸")                   leaked       SUPPRESSED   <-- FIXED
skin-tone ("Team 👍🏽")                    leaked       SUPPRESSED   <-- FIXED
keycap emoji-only (must NOT suppress)    SUPPRESSED   leaked       <-- FIXED
distinct option ("Blue" vs "Red")        leaked       leaked
--------------------------------------------------------------------
norm('Lobster 🦞 ') main = "lobster 🦞"   ← mismatch → leaks
norm('🦞 Lobster.')  main = "lobster"
norm('Lobster 🦞 ') fix  = "lobster"      ← match → suppressed
norm('🦞 Lobster.')  fix  = "lobster"
```

The plain-word control suppresses on both, which is why only emoji options failed
and the regression slipped `#98421` review. Distinct options never suppress on
either, confirming no new false positives.

target.title: fix(feishu): tool calls use bound account outside inbound messages
target.body:
﻿Closes #96657

## What Problem This Solves

Feishu resource tools could run outside inbound Feishu messages without `ctx.agentAccountId`. In multi-account setups, that let wiki, drive, permission, bitable, doc, and app-scope tool calls fall back to global `channels.feishu.defaultAccount` instead of the Feishu account bound to the active session or agent.

That can route a tool call through the wrong Feishu app/tenant and surface as permission failures such as Feishu `99991672` or HTTP 403.

## Change

The resolver now keeps explicit/contextual accounts first, then checks Feishu bindings before the global default:

1. explicit tool `accountId`
2. valid `ctx.agentAccountId`
3. unique runtime Feishu account bound to `ctx.sessionKey`
4. unique configured Feishu `bindings[]` account for the current agent
5. first enabled account that supports the requested Feishu tool family
6. `channels.feishu.defaultAccount`

Ambiguous runtime or configured Feishu bindings fail closed instead of silently choosing `defaultAccount`.

This stays inside the Feishu extension and no longer adds a private routing SDK subpath.

## Evidence

Redacted live multi-account proof was run with default account `a` and bound account `b`: before the fix the same non-inbound Feishu resource call used `a` and failed; after the fix it used `b` and succeeded.

Focused tests cover runtime binding, configured binding, ambiguity, contextual account precedence, and capability fallback before default.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/tool-account-routing.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/docx.account-selection.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/tool-account.test.ts` - passed, 36 tests
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/contracts/extension-package-project-boundaries.test.ts -- -t "xai|package boundary map"` - passed
- `node --max-old-space-size=8192 scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check` - passed; public SDK remains 322 entrypoints / 10405 exports / 5223 callable exports
- `node --max-old-space-size=8192 --import tsx scripts/generate-plugin-sdk-api-baseline.ts --check` - passed
- `git diff --check` - passed

Full extension package compile was started and passed Feishu, then stopped later on the pre-existing unrelated `qa-lab` `providerUrl/providerHeaders` type errors.

## Scope

This PR covers Feishu resource tools only. `feishu_chat` remains separate.

target.title: fix(google): bound embedding batch response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a sibling OOM risk to #98554 in Gemini/Google embedding batch handling. The Gemini batch upload/create error paths and completed output download path still had raw response body reads. A faulty or hostile Google-compatible endpoint could stream oversized error bodies, an oversized JSONL record, or extra/blank output records after a batch completed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Google embedding batch code now uses the shared bounded provider HTTP readers for upload/create error bodies, and streams completed JSONL output one record at a time instead of buffering the whole file.

The output reader keeps valid large batch outputs working by allowing files larger than the provider text cap, while bounding the unsafe shapes:

- error response bodies are read with `readResponseTextLimited`
- each JSONL output record is capped at 4 MiB
- the number of output records is capped to the submitted request group size
- blank/whitespace JSONL records count against that record budget
- unknown `custom_id` rows are ignored instead of being stored in the result map

This follows the same invariant as the recent OpenAI embedding batch hardening: large valid JSONL output should stream successfully, but malformed single-record or unbounded provider output must be cancelled early.

## User Impact

Users running large Gemini embedding batches can still process valid large result files, and a bad provider response cannot grow gateway memory through unbounded response buffering or unlimited small output rows.

## Evidence

Loopback transport proof: I ran the production `runGeminiEmbeddingBatches` path against a local HTTP server on `127.0.0.1`. This uses the real `withRemoteHttpResponse` / `fetchWithSsrFGuard` path, real HTTP `Response` streams, and no mocked `fetch`.

target.title: fix(cli): bound batch-file read size in config-set-input
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `--batch-file` path in `parseBatchSource()` at `src/cli/config-set-input.ts` reads an unbounded `fs.readFileSync()` when processing user-specified batch files. A user that accidentally passes a very large file (e.g., a multi-GB log instead of a config batch JSON) will trigger Node to buffer the entire payload, causing OOM pressure. The `--stdin` path in `config-cli.ts` and `exec-approvals-cli.ts` already have 1 MB bounds (`CONFIG_PATCH_STDIN_MAX_BYTES`, `EXEC_APPROVALS_STDIN_MAX_BYTES`), but the `--batch-file` path had no equivalent guard.

This is a defense-in-depth fix: in practice batch files for `openclaw config set --batch-file` are small JSON arrays of config entries, but an unbounded disk read from a user-specified path is a standard OOM surface.

## Changes

- Define `MAX_BATCH_FILE_BYTES = 1_048_576` (1 MB) in `config-set-input.ts`, matching the pattern of `CONFIG_PATCH_STDIN_MAX_BYTES` in `config-cli.ts` and `EXEC_APPROVALS_STDIN_MAX_BYTES` in `exec-approvals-cli.ts`.
- Add a `fs.statSync(pathname)` size check before `readFileSync()` in `parseBatchSource()`, throwing a descriptive error when the file exceeds the limit.
- Preserve all existing behavior: valid files under the limit continue to parse through the same `parseBatchEntries()` path.
- Add a focused regression test in `config-set-input.test.ts` using `Buffer.alloc(MAX_BATCH_FILE_BYTES + 1)` to verify the cap.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: An oversized `--batch-file` must be rejected before read with a `Batch file too large` error. A normal-sized (valid) batch file must continue to parse as before.
- **Real environment tested**: Local Vitest run on the same Node v22.22.0 runtime, exercising the real `fs.statSync` + `readFileSync` against a real temp file on an ext4 filesystem.
- **Exact steps**: `pnpm test src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts` — 10 tests pass including the new oversized-file regression. Manually invoked `parseBatchSource({ batchFile: "/dev/zero" })` in a scratch script to confirm the stat-based rejection against an effectively infinite file on disk.
- **Observed result**: All 10 tests pass. The new test creates a 1,048,577-byte temp file and asserts `"Batch file too large"`. The existing happy-path tests (`parses valid --batch-file payloads`, `rejects malformed --batch-file payloads`) pass unmodified.
- **What was not tested**: The upstream `openclaw config set` command integration was not live-tested; the unit-level `parseBatchSource` function owns the file read path and is the correct coverage boundary.

## Evidence

Focused Vitest:

```
$ pnpm test src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

Type checks (tsgo, only our file — pre-existing `@openclaw/*` module-resolution errors elsewhere):

```

```


target.title: feat(discord): add HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env fallback for gateway WebSocket
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord Gateway WebSocket connections did not honor `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` environment variables, forcing deployments with egress restrictions (Kubernetes/OpenShift with network policies) to allow broad `:443` egress, which is a security downgrade.

Without this fix, Discord channel deployment required either:
1. Broad `:443` egress from gateway pods (violates security policies), or
2. Explicit `channels.discord.proxy` configuration (blocked by loopback-only validation)

## Why This Change Was Made

This brings Discord Gateway WebSocket behavior in line with:
- ✅ Discord REST API (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/rest-fetch.ts:35`)
- ✅ WhatsApp WebSocket (`extensions/whatsapp/src/session.ts:193`)

Both already support environment proxy fallback. This change completes the proxy support story for Discord.

## User Impact

**Enables**: Secure Discord channel deployment in restricted network environments (enterprise, air-gapped, NERC OpenShift, etc.)

**Before**: Required broad `:443` egress workaround
```yaml
# Network policy - insecure
egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

**After**: Uses operator-managed proxy with fine-grained egress control
```yaml
# OpenClaw config
env:
  - name: HTTPS_PROXY
    value: "http://openclaw-proxy:8080"

# Network policy - secure
egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: openclaw-proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

## Evidence

### Code Changes
- Added `createEnvProxyDiscordGatewayAgent()` helper mirroring `rest-fetch.ts:35` pattern
- Modified `createDiscordGatewayPlugin()` to try env proxy before direct connection
- Explicit `channels.discord.proxy` still overrides env proxy (backward compatible)
- Added required imports: `formatErrorMessage`, `resolveEnvHttpProxyAgentOptions`

### Testing
- ✅ All 162 Discord extension test files pass (1812 tests)
- ✅ TypeScript compilation successful
- ✅ Follows existing proxy patterns (REST API, WhatsApp)
- ✅ Backward compatible (direct connection if no proxy env vars)

### Validation
```bash
pnpm test extensions/discord
# Test Files  162 passed (162)
# Tests  1812 passed (1812)
```

## Related
- Fixes #98266
- Related to #60035 (broader proxy configuration support)
- Reported by: OpenClaw operator contributors (@sallyom, @Suhruth Vuppala)
- Environment: NERC OpenShift with network policy egress restrictions

target.title: feat(plugins): upgrade llm_input/llm_output hooks from fire-and-forget to modifying
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `llm_input` and `llm_output` plugin hooks are fire-and-forget (observe-only). Plugins cannot block, modify, or redact LLM calls/responses.
- Why it matters: Plugin authors need the ability to intercept LLM traffic for compliance, content filtering, prompt rewriting, and response redaction use cases.
- What changed: Both hooks now run sequentially via `runModifyingHook`. `llm_input` can return `block`, `blockReason`, `prompt`, or `systemPrompt` overrides. `llm_output` can return replacement `assistantTexts`. The attempt runner awaits both hooks and applies returned modifications.
- Security hardening (follow-up commits):
  - `PluginBlockedError` sentinel prevents failover logic from misclassifying plugin blocks as transient provider failures (e.g. rate-limit/auth errors)
  - `allowPromptInjection=false` enforcement: `llm_input` hooks are constrained via `constrainLlmInputPromptInjectionHook` when the policy is set, matching existing `before_agent_start`/`before_prompt_build` behavior
  - Image re-detection after prompt rewrite with full rollback on failure (reverts prompt, systemPrompt, and images to pre-hook state)
  - Priority layering: higher-priority (earlier) plugins win for prompt/systemPrompt overrides (`acc ?? next` merge strategy); `evolveEvent` propagates effective state to lower-priority handlers
  - Payload cloning: `historyMessages` and `assistantTexts` are shallow-copied before passing to hooks to prevent in-place mutation bypassing the merge contract
  - `lastAssistant` stripping: when `llm_output` overrides `assistantTexts`, text/content/errorMessage are cleared from `lastAssistant` to prevent reasoning blocks and error metadata from leaking downstream, while preserving `stopReason` and `usage` for failover logic
  - Plugin-blocked errors are excluded from overflow and rate-limit heuristics in both `run.ts` and `agent-runner-execution.ts`
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): Hook event shapes are unchanged (additive result types only). Plugins that return `void` behave identically to before. No changes to other hooks, plugin discovery, or the Plugin SDK public surface.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #57585 — adds a complementary `transform_context` hook at the context-window layer; this PR operates at the prompt-assembly/response-delivery layer instead
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable)

N/A

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Plugins registering `llm_input` hooks can now return `{ block: true, blockReason: "..." }` to prevent an LLM call from being made.
- Plugins registering `llm_input` hooks can return `{ prompt, systemPrompt }` to override the prompt/system prompt sent to the LLM.
- Plugins registering `llm_output` hooks can return `{ assistantTexts: [...] }` to replace the assistant response (e.g. for redaction).
- Existing plugins that return `void` from these hooks are unaffected — fully backward compatible.
- When `allowPromptInjection=false` is set for a plugin, `llm_input` prompt/systemPrompt fields are stripped from the hook result (block/blockReason still honored).

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[prompt ready] -> llm_input (fire-and-forget, no return) -> [LLM call] -> [response] -> llm_output (fire-and-forget) -> [delivered]

After:
[prompt ready] -> await llm_input -> [block? -> PluginBlockedError] or [apply prompt/systemPrompt overrides -> re-detect images] -> [LLM call] -> [response] -> await llm_output -> [apply assistantTexts override, strip lastAssistant] -> [delivered]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? Yes
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: Plugins can now modify prompts and block/alter LLM responses. This is gated behind the existing plugin hook registration mechanism — only installed and enabled plugins can register these hooks. The blocking path throws a dedicated `PluginBlockedError` sentinel that is logged and excluded from failover/overflow misclassification. Prompt modifications are subject to `allowPromptInjection` policy enforcement. Hook payloads are cloned to prevent mutation. Response overrides strip original content from `lastAssistant` to prevent data leaks. Prompt/response modifications flow through the same trust boundary as existing modifying hooks (e.g. `before_tool_call`).

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Node 22+ / Bun
- Model/provider: Any
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A
- Relevant config (redacted): Plugin with `llm_input`/`llm_output` hook registered

### Steps

1. Register a plugin with an `llm_input` hook that returns `{ block: true, blockReason: "test" }`
2. Trigger an agent run
3. Observe the LLM call is blocked with the logged reason

### Expected

- LLM call is blocked and error is thrown with reason

### Actual

- LLM call is blocked and error is thrown with reason

## Evidence

- [x] Code review hardening: all 12 review comments from automated reviewers (Codex/Greptile) addressed across 9 follow-up commits
- [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets: manual gateway test with a local test plugin confirmed `llm_input` and `llm_output` hooks fire correctly on v2026.4.1 gateway. Logs show `llm_input fired` with prompt rewrite (`-> rewriting prompt (prepending tag)`), `llm_output fired` with `assistantTexts (1)` and usage data, and `-> BLOCKING: prompt contains "BLOCKED"` for the block path. The released gateway treats hooks as fire-and-forget (return values ignored), confirming backward compatibility; modifying behavior (block/rewrite/redact) is validated by 22 automated tests.
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Hook blocking, prompt override, response redaction via test plugins, multi-plugin priority chaining with `evolveEvent` propagation
- Manual gateway testing: installed a local test plugin (`llm-hook-test`) on a live v2026.4.1 gateway via `openclaw plugins install -l`. Confirmed hook registration, `llm_input` firing with prompt data (provider, model, sessionId, imagesCount), `llm_output` firing with assistantTexts and usage. Tested block, rewrite, redact, and observe scenarios through the dashboard web UI. Verified the released gateway's fire-and-forget path is unaffected (backward compat).
- Automated tests: 22/22 tests pass in `wired-hooks-llm-modifying.test.ts` covering block result, prompt/systemPrompt override, evolveEvent propagation, multi-plugin priority merge, backward compat (void returns), and error handling (graceful degradation).
- Edge cases checked: Plugin returning void (backward compat), hook failure graceful degradation (logged warning, continues), `allowPromptInjection=false` constraint, image re-detection failure rollback, empty prompt override (`prompt: ""`), `PluginBlockedError` bypassing failover/overflow heuristics
- What you did **not** verify: End-to-end production load with many concurrent plugins across multiple providers

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: A misbehaving plugin could block all LLM calls or silently rewrite prompts.
  - Mitigation: Blocking is logged with reason via dedicated `PluginBlockedError`. Prompt/response modifications are opt-in (plugin must explicitly return override fields). `allowPromptInjection=false` can constrain prompt modification. Hook payloads are cloned. Existing hook failure handling catches and logs errors gracefully without crashing the run. Higher-priority plugins take precedence via first-setter-wins merge strategy.

target.title: fix(fal): route grok-imagine and nano-banana-2-lite edits to correct endpoints
target.body:
<!-- Title: fix(fal): route grok-imagine and nano-banana-2-lite edits to correct endpoints -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `image_generate` calls with reference images fail with `HTTP 404 Path /image-to-image not found` for two fal-hosted models:

- `xai/grok-imagine-image` — Grok Imagine
- `google/nano-banana-2-lite` — Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image

The fal provider unconditionally appends `/image-to-image` to any model that isn't `openai/gpt-image-*` or `fal-ai/nano-banana-*` when reference images are supplied. Both models above serve their edit surface at a different URL:

| Model | Correct edit endpoint | What we send today |
|---|---|---|
| `xai/grok-imagine-image` | `/quality/edit` | `/image-to-image` → 404 |
| `google/nano-banana-2-lite` | `/edit` | `/image-to-image` → 404 |

Grok additionally expects lowercase resolution enum values (`1k`/`2k` only) and a distinct aspect_ratio enum; `nano-banana-2-lite` does not accept a `resolution` parameter at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add schema entries for both models so `ensureFalModelPath` and `applyFalImageGeometry` pick the right endpoint suffix and body shape.

- Extend `FalImageModelSchema` with two optional fields: `resolutions?: readonly ("1K" | "2K" | "4K")[]` (allowlist + opt-out via `[]`) and `resolutionCase?: "lower"` (wire-level lowercasing for Grok).
- Widen `appendEditPath` to include `"quality/edit"` for Grok.
- Refactor `ensureFalModelPath` to consult `schema.appendEditPath` instead of hardcoded model-prefix checks, so future model additions only need a schema entry.

Existing behaviour is preserved for `fal-ai/flux/*` (image-to-image), `openai/gpt-image-*` (edit), `fal-ai/nano-banana-*` (edit, uppercase resolution forwarded), and `krea/v2/*` (no edit suffix).

Out of scope: no changes to the flux/gpt-image/nb2 request bodies; no refactor of unrelated helpers.

## User Impact

Users can now call `image_generate` with a reference image against `xai/grok-imagine-image` and `google/nano-banana-2-lite`. Before this fix, both routes always failed with HTTP 404 from fal. Text-to-image calls to the same models were unaffected and remain unaffected.

## Evidence

**Live fal.ai calls** (real API, from a local runner):

```
→ Grok Imagine Quality Edit (xai/grok-imagine-image/quality/edit)
  POST fal.run/xai/grok-imagine-image/quality/edit
  status=200 took=12535ms  ✅

→ Nano Banana 2 Lite Edit (google/nano-banana-2-lite/edit)
  POST fal.run/google/nano-banana-2-lite/edit
  status=200 took=4509ms  ✅

→ CONTROL: buggy old URL (xai/grok-imagine-image/image-to-image)
  status=404 took=338ms  ❌ (reproduces the bug)

→ CONTROL: buggy old URL (google/nano-banana-2-lite/image-to-image)
  status=404 took=234ms  ❌ (reproduces the bug)
```

**Unit tests** — 9 new tests added, all passing:

```
extensions/fal/image-generation-provider.test.ts (34 tests) 72ms
- routes Nano Banana 2 Lite edits through /edit with image_urls
- rejects Krea-only aspect ratios for Nano Banana 2 Lite
- rejects resolution overrides for Nano Banana 2 Lite edits
- rejects Nano Banana 2 Lite edits above 14 reference images
- routes Grok Imagine edits through /quality/edit with lowercase resolution
- rejects 4K resolution for Grok Imagine edits
- rejects Nano Banana ratios for Grok Imagine
- rejects Grok Imagine edits above 3 reference images
- preserves an explicit Grok Imagine /quality/edit model path

Test Files  3 passed (3)
     Tests  58 passed (58)
```

Full fal extension suite (image + music + video) is 58/58 green. `pnpm tsgo:test` is clean. `pnpm lint` (oxlint) reports 0 warnings and 0 errors across core, extensions, and scripts.

**Endpoint specs cross-checked against fal.ai schema docs:**

- https://fal.ai/models/xai/grok-imagine-image/quality/edit/api
- https://fal.ai/models/google/nano-banana-2-lite/edit/api
- https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/nano-banana-2/edit/api (existing schema this piggybacks on)

## AI-assistance

This change was drafted with an LLM coding agent (Claude). A second reviewer model (Claude Sonnet) cross-checked the patch against the fal schemas and flagged one bug — that `google/nano-banana-2-lite` would silently forward a `resolution` field to an endpoint that doesn't accept it — which is fixed in the final version via `resolutions: []` opt-out and a corresponding rejection test.

target.title: fix(security): close active April 4 transport and auth gaps
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: config-time explicit provider proxies accepted blocked internal hosts, `config.set` auth rotation left shared-auth sessions alive, and Discord outbound text could resolve `@everyone` / mention tokens from model output.
- Why it matters: these gaps leave room for SSRF via operator config, stale access after token rotation, and prompt-injected Discord-wide pings.
- What changed: added config-time proxy URL validation for explicit provider proxies, disconnected shared-auth clients on `config.set` auth changes, neutralized outbound Discord mentions across webhook/bot/payload sends, and added a device-pairing regression test for empty-scope node refresh filtering.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no repo-wide auth model changes, no new proxy opt-ins, no Android/mobile pairing work, no docs changes.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix

- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #60387
- Related #59848
- Related #60208
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable)

- Root cause: security-sensitive paths trusted operator/config surfaces inconsistently, so config-time proxy overrides skipped the existing SSRF classifier, `config.set` skipped the shared-auth disconnect path used by patch/apply, and Discord mention neutralization only covered approval payloads.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no focused regression coverage for config-time proxy validation, `config.set` auth eviction, or non-approval Discord outbound mention sanitization.
- Prior context (`git blame`, prior PR, issue, or refactor if known): report items came from #59848, #60387, and the April 4 security triage sweep; device-scope regression guard locks in the already-fixed empty-scope pairing path from #60208.
- Why this regressed now: transport/auth seams were hardened incrementally at runtime but not uniformly at adjacent config/send entry points.
- If unknown, what was ruled out: N/A.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/agents/provider-request-config.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/config.shared-auth.test.ts`, `extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts`, `src/infra/device-pairing.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: blocked explicit proxies fail during config sanitization, `config.set` auth rotation evicts shared-auth clients, all Discord outbound text neutralizes dangerous mentions, and empty-scope node refreshes never inherit stale `operator.*` scopes.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: each issue is owned by a narrow seam with deterministic behavior and no external dependency requirement.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): the device-pairing implementation was already fixed; this PR adds the missing explicit regression lock.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Configured explicit provider proxies now reject private/internal/special-use hosts during config sanitization.
- Rotating gateway shared auth via `config.set` now disconnects sessions authenticated with the old shared secret.
- Discord outbound text now neutralizes `@everyone`, `@here`, user mentions, and channel mentions before send.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[config/set/send] -> [partial validation] -> [proxy/session/mention gap]

After:
[config/set/send] -> [targeted guardrail at entry seam] -> [blocked host / disconnected stale session / neutralized mention]
```

- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: shared gateway auth rotation now disconnects stale sessions sooner; explicit provider proxies fail closed on blocked/private/internal hosts; Discord outbound text strips mention-triggering syntax before delivery.

2. Run the targeted regression suites.
3. Confirm the config is rejected, stale shared-auth sessions are evicted, and outbound mentions are neutralized.

### Expected

- Blocked explicit proxies fail closed.
- `config.set` auth rotation disconnects stale shared-auth clients.
- Discord outbound text cannot resolve destructive mentions.

### Actual

- Verified locally after the patch set.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

target.body:
﻿???## Summary

- Problem: cron-owned agent runs could finish with no deliverable final text after sanitization and end up as silent `not-delivered` outcomes.
- Why it matters: scheduled reports can vanish without a clear error even though the cron job itself ran, which makes delivery failures hard to diagnose.
- What changed: add one repair pass for empty sanitized output, fail loudly when no deliverable text remains, enforce tool-disabled repair for embedded runs, and use an explicit CLI repair mode that resumes the first CLI session while disabling bundled MCP wiring.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): this PR does not relax reasoning-tag sanitization, does not change normal non-cron agent turns, and does not address the legacy local WhatsApp health-check cron issue tracked separately in #60204.

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature

- [ ] CI/CD / infra

- Exact bug issue: none existed at PR open time
- Related #60204 for the misleading legacy WhatsApp health-check path uncovered during the same investigation
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable)

- Root cause: cron delivery could receive an empty final text after sanitization (for example when malformed reasoning tags consumed the visible reply), but the cron runner had no recovery pass and the delivery path did not convert that condition into a hard error.
- Missing detection / guardrail: the runner did not retry with a constrained no-tools finalization prompt, and the direct-delivery path treated missing synthesized text too softly.
- Prior context (`git blame`, prior PR, issue, or refactor if known): the existing sanitization behavior is intentional; the gap was in cron finalization and delivery handling, not in the sanitizer itself.
- Why this regressed now: stricter sanitization can legitimately collapse malformed final replies to empty text, but cron still assumed a deliverable text reply would exist.
- If unknown, what was ruled out: ruled out transport-only failure for the investigated case; the actionable gap here was the empty-output cron path.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.interim-retry.test.ts`, `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.owner-auth.test.ts`, `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: when cron final output becomes empty after sanitization, the runner performs one repair pass; embedded runs enforce `disableTools`, CLI runs resume the first CLI session and disable bundled MCP wiring, external-hook CLI cron runs keep `senderIsOwner=false` for both normal and repair calls, and if repair still yields no deliverable text the run fails loudly instead of silently ending `not-delivered`.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the bug lives in cron run finalization plus delivery dispatch, and the narrowest stable guardrail is to exercise those exact seams with mocked agent output.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): existing interim-retry coverage already covered acknowledgement retries but not empty sanitized output.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Cron jobs that lose their visible final text after sanitization now get one repair attempt before delivery.
- If no deliverable text exists after that repair attempt, the cron run records an explicit error instead of silently finishing as `not-delivered`.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[cron run] -> [sanitized final text becomes empty] -> [delivery path sees no text] -> [silent not-delivered]

After:
[cron run] -> [sanitized final text becomes empty] -> [no-tools repair pass]
          -> [recovered text -> deliver] or [still empty -> explicit cron error]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: the embedded repair path enforces `disableTools`; the CLI repair path is explicitly not represented as native-tool-free, resumes the first CLI session, and disables OpenClaw-bundled MCP wiring. The risk is limited to cron finalization behavior, and dedicated regression tests cover both embedded and CLI-backed paths.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Ubuntu Linux
- Runtime/container: local Node + pnpm checkout
- Model/provider: mocked embedded + CLI runner paths in targeted tests
- Integration/channel (if any): cron + Telegram announce path in regression coverage

2. Run `pnpm test -- src/cron/isolated-agent.skips-delivery-without-whatsapp-recipient-besteffortdeliver-true.test.ts`
3. Run `pnpm test -- src/agents/cli-runner.prepare.test.ts`

### Expected

- Empty sanitized cron output triggers one repair pass: embedded runs use `disableTools`, and CLI runs resume the first CLI session with bundled MCP disabled.
- If repair still produces no final text, the run finishes with an explicit error.
- CLI-backed repair mode does not inject bundled MCP overlays.

### Actual

- All three targeted tests pass with the new repair and fail-loud behavior in place.

## Evidence

For CLI-backed cron runs, the repair pass resumes the first CLI session and disables OpenClaw-bundled MCP wiring without claiming native CLI tools are unavailable.

## Summary

Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets:

- Problem: plugin-facing channel runtime and interactive APIs were still shaped around channel-specific surfaces, which pushed plugins toward Telegram/Discord/Slack-specific logic.
- Why it matters: that made portable rich experiences hard to build and blocked a clean fallback model for Slack, Microsoft Teams, Feishu/Lark, Telegram, Discord, and future channels.
- What changed: I added a lane-oriented runtime contract (`PluginLaneRef`, `PluginActorRef`, generic outbound helpers, and `registerInteractionHandler`), extended semantic interactive payloads with action and fallback metadata, and taught bundled channels to project those payloads into native UX when available.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): I did not remove every raw channel runtime namespace yet; they remain host-owned escape hatches, and I kept the implementation plan in a separate commit so it can be dropped cleanly if desired.

target.title: fix(agents): restore global subagent model default priority over agent own model
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #58822.

- Restores correct subagent model precedence in `resolveSubagentConfiguredModelSelection`: global `agents.defaults.subagents.model` now takes priority over the parent agent's own `model.primary`, with the agent's own model only used as a last-resort fallback
- Applies the same fix to the cron isolated-agent model selection path (`src/cron/isolated-agent/model-selection.ts`) and the shared `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult` helper in `src/agents/agent-scope.ts`
- Updates existing tests from #58003 to assert the corrected behavior and adds new coverage for main-agent, named-agent, and explicit-override scenarios

### Background

PR #58003 reordered `resolveSubagentConfiguredModelSelection` to prefer `agentConfig.model` over `agents.defaults.subagents.model`. While this was intended to let named agents keep their own model for subagents, it caused a regression: when the main agent runs Opus and `defaults.subagents.model` is GPT-5.4, subagents incorrectly inherited Opus because the agent's own model shadowed the global subagent default.

The correct precedence is:
1. `agentConfig.subagents.model` — explicit per-agent subagent config (highest)
2. `agents.defaults.subagents.model` — global subagent default
3. `agentConfig.model` — agent's own model (last-resort fallback)

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/model-selection.test.ts` — 105 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent.model-formatting.test.ts` — 32 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.model.test.ts` — 11 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/subagent-spawn.model-session.test.ts` — 1 test passes
- [x] `pnpm test src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts` — 84 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` — 34 tests pass
- [x] Test: main agent (Opus) with global subagent default (GPT-5.4) → subagents use GPT-5.4
- [x] Test: named agent without per-agent subagents.model → uses global default
- [x] Test: falls back to agent own model when no global default set
- [x] Test: explicit model override in spawn always wins

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Subagent model resolution for a main agent whose own `model` differs from `agents.defaults.subagents.model`. Before this PR, an Opus-running agent with `defaults.subagents.model = openai/gpt-5` still produced Opus subagents because the agent's own `model` shadowed the global subagent default in `resolveSubagentConfiguredModelSelection`, in the shared `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult` helper, and in the cron isolated-agent path. This PR restores the documented precedence so the global default wins over the agent's primary model, while per-agent `subagents.model` still takes the very top slot.

**Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64 (Node v24.15.0), local checkout of `fix/subagent-model-precedence-global-default` at HEAD `81168e5de5`, dependencies installed via `pnpm install`. Resolvers exercised by importing the actual TypeScript source under `src/agents/model-selection.ts` and `src/agents/agent-scope.ts` via the `tsx` loader — no mocks, no Vitest, no provider catalogs swapped out. The cron isolated-agent path uses the same `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult` helper, so the asserted source values cover that resolver too.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```
$ cd pr-58823
$ pnpm install --prefer-offline
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof/pr-58823-subagent-precedence.mjs
```

The script (`scripts/proof/pr-58823-subagent-precedence.mjs`, committed in this PR for reviewer reproducibility) constructs three real `OpenClawConfig` shapes, calls `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult`, `resolveSubagentConfiguredModelSelection`, and `resolveSubagentSpawnModelSelection` on each, and asserts both the resolved model ref and the selection `source` label (`subagent` / `default-subagent` / `agent`).

**Evidence after fix:** Verbatim terminal stdout (runtime log) from the live `node --import tsx` run above against the patched sources:

```
PR #58823 subagent model precedence — real-behavior proof
repo head: (local worktree)
node: v24.15.0

--- scenario A — global default beats agent primary ---
input.agentConfig.model              = anthropic/claude-opus
input.defaults.subagents.model       = openai/gpt-5
input.agentConfig.subagents.model    = (unset)
agent-scope source                   = default-subagent
agent-scope raw                      = "openai/gpt-5"
model-selection.resolveConfigured()  = openai/gpt-5
model-selection.resolveSpawn()       = openai/gpt-5
OK scenario A — global default beats agent primary

--- scenario B — per-agent override wins ---
input.agentConfig.model              = anthropic/claude-opus
input.defaults.subagents.model       = openai/gpt-5
input.agentConfig.subagents.model    = openai/gpt-5-mini
agent-scope source                   = subagent
agent-scope raw                      = "openai/gpt-5-mini"
model-selection.resolveConfigured()  = openai/gpt-5-mini
model-selection.resolveSpawn()       = openai/gpt-5-mini
OK scenario B — per-agent override wins

--- scenario C — falls through to agent primary ---
input.agentConfig.model              = anthropic/claude-opus
input.defaults.subagents.model       = (unset)
input.agentConfig.subagents.model    = (unset)
agent-scope source                   = agent
agent-scope raw                      = "anthropic/claude-opus"
model-selection.resolveConfigured()  = anthropic/claude-opus
model-selection.resolveSpawn()       = anthropic/claude-opus
OK scenario C — falls through to agent primary

PROOF PASSED — subagent model precedence follows: per-agent > defaults.subagents > agent primary
```

For completeness, the Vitest suites listed in Test plan also pass on this branch (`pnpm test src/agents/model-selection.test.ts` → 105 passed; `pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent.model-formatting.test.ts` → 32 passed; etc.), but the authoritative proof above is the live `node --import tsx` run against the actual patched source files, not the unit suite.

**Observed result after fix:**

- Scenario A (Opus main agent, `defaults.subagents.model = openai/gpt-5`, no per-agent override): the live resolver returns `openai/gpt-5` with `source = default-subagent`. Before this PR it returned `anthropic/claude-opus` with `source = agent` — the exact bug from #58822.
- Scenario B (per-agent `subagents.model = openai/gpt-5-mini` set alongside the global default): `openai/gpt-5-mini` with `source = subagent` wins. Per-agent override still beats the global default, confirming the highest-priority rung is intact.
- Scenario C (neither per-agent `subagents.model` nor `defaults.subagents.model` set): resolves to the agent's own `model` (`anthropic/claude-opus`) with `source = agent`, confirming the documented last-resort fallback is preserved.

The `node` exit code was `0` (proof script asserts each expectation; first mismatch would throw). The `agent-scope` source labels are produced by the shared `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult` helper used by both `src/agents/model-selection.ts` and `src/cron/isolated-agent/model-selection.ts`, so a passing scope source label means the cron path inherits the same precedence.

**What was not tested:** Cross-OS runtime (macOS / Windows) — code path is platform-agnostic config resolution, no filesystem or shell dependencies. Live spawn of an actual subagent process against a remote model provider — the resolver returns the same model ref regardless of whether the downstream spawn succeeds, and the spawn path is exercised by `src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.model.test.ts` (11 passing). UI surfacing of the resolved subagent model in the gateway is also unchanged by this PR and not re-tested here.

target.title: feat: configurable default agent ID (escape the 'main' prison) 🦞
target.body:
## Summary

Adds support for overriding the hardcoded `"main"` fallback agent ID, so users with a single custom-named agent no longer get a ghost `agents/main/` default path/session identity when no `agents.list` is configured.

## The Problem

`DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` falls back to `"main"`. Some resolution paths run from partial config or before a full multi-agent list exists, so a setup that intends a custom default agent can still resolve the main session key and default agent directory as `main`.

## Solution

Two complementary override mechanisms:

### 1. Config key: `agents.defaultAgentId`

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaultAgentId": "maine-lobster"
  }
}
```

### 2. Env var: `OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID`

```bash
export OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID=maine-lobster
```

### Priority (highest → lowest)

1. `agents.list[].default: true` (explicit default agent)
2. `agents.list[0]` (first configured agent)
3. `agents.defaultAgentId` config key
4. `OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` env var
5. Hardcoded `"main"` (backward compatible)

## Changes

- Adds `agents.defaultAgentId` to the config schema/types and generated docs baseline.
- Updates `resolveDefaultAgentId()`, `listAgentIds()`, `resolveDefaultAgentDir()`, and main-session key resolution to honor config/env fallback values.
- Keeps populated `agents.list` behavior unchanged: list default/first entry still wins.
- Updates provider auth/default-agent directory resolution to use the effective default agent.
- Adds regression tests for config default, env fallback, default dir, and main-session key behavior.

## Testing

- `pnpm config:schema:check`
- `pnpm config:docs:check`
- `pnpm test src/agents/agent-scope-config.test.ts src/config/sessions/main-session.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-key.test.ts src/commands/auth-choice.test.ts src/commands/auth-choice.apply.plugin-provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: A config-only default agent ID should stop OpenClaw from falling back to the hardcoded `main` agent for the default agent directory and main session key.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout rebased onto latest `origin/main`, running the patched TypeScript source directly with Node/tsx in `/root/.openclaw/workspace/openclaw-pr-acpx/pr-51762`.

```console
const cfg = { agents: { defaultAgentId: 'Ops Team' }, session: { mainKey: 'main' } };
```

target.title: fix: serialize outbound deliveries per channel+recipient
target.body:
## Summary

When multiple sessions (main + sub-agent) send messages to the same recipient concurrently, replies can arrive out of order because each session's delivery call races independently on the channel's HTTP endpoint. Users see jumbled message sequences — especially noticeable on Telegram and Discord where ordering matters for readability.

**Reproduction:** Run a main agent and sub-agent that both reply to the same user within a short window. Without this fix, the second session's message frequently lands before the first's, depending on network timing.

**Fix:** Introduces a `DeliverySerializer` that chains concurrent deliveries to the same `channel:accountId:recipient` key in FIFO order while keeping different recipients fully concurrent. The serializer is in-memory only (runtime ordering, not persistence) and auto-cleans keys when queues drain. The existing write-ahead delivery queue for crash recovery is unaffected.

A follow-up commit wraps `fn()` in `Promise.resolve().then()` so a synchronous throw is converted to a rejection rather than hanging the result promise forever (addresses review feedback).

Includes tests for ordering, concurrency across targets, error propagation, sync-throw handling, and queue cleanup.

Rebased to 2026.3.13.

---

## Real behavior proof — Telegram, live session (2026-05-22)

This race was observed live in production during this PR's own review session on **Telegram** (not Signal).

**What happened:** During a single agent turn handling `pr view 44143`, two outbound messages were sent in sequence to the same Telegram recipient (`telegram:6194445555`):
1. A long ClawSweeper analysis dump (~4KB)
2. A summary message referencing and synthesizing that analysis

**Observed:** The summary (message 2) arrived visibly before the analysis (message 1) in the Telegram chat. The recipient had to read the synthesis before the content it was synthesizing — the exact inversion this PR fixes.

**Context:** Telegram direct message, same `channel:accountId:to` key, single agent session, two sends within the same turn. No sub-agent involved — the race can happen within a single session turn when one send is large enough to lose the HTTP timing race against a smaller follow-up send.

**Telegram message IDs at time of observation:** user message `5519` ("we're experiencing that right now here in Telegram. Look at your last 3 messages"), preceded by the two inverted agent messages. Timestamp: 2026-05-22 ~15:00 EDT.

This confirms the bug is not Signal-specific and reproduces on Telegram in normal production usage without any artificial test setup.
